name: Russel E. Heacock's House, Monroe Street

documented_range.note: BUILT IN THE SPRING OF 1835, WHICH IS INSIDE THE SCENE YEAR AND BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Andreas: 'In the spring of 1835, he built a house on what he supposed was his lot, only to find that he was on Monroe Street, not Adams, whither he proceeded to remove it on rollers.' The house, its season, its owner and the fact that it was moved a block are all documented. The range opens on 1835-03-01 as the earliest reading of 'the spring'.

change_note: The building as this dataset can state it on the scene date. Where the sources give a size, a plan or a fabric, the record carries it; where they do not, the note says so attribute by attribute.

placement.position_note: OUTSIDE THE MODELLED GROUND, AND THE DATE OF THE MOVE IS UNKNOWN. Two things are invented here. First, WHICH STREET IT STOOD ON on 1 July 1835: Andreas gives no date for the removal, so the house may have been on Monroe or already on Adams. This record puts it on Monroe, where it was built, because that is the position the source actually states. Second, WHERE ON MONROE: nothing says. The northing is estimated from the plat module - the block pitch implied by the reconstruction recipes' Randolph-to-Washington bands, carried two blocks further south - and lands about 215 m beyond the southern edge of the e1834_harbor_cut heightfield, so the phase declares ground_contact: outside_modelled_ground. THE BUILDING IS IN THE DATASET AND NOT UNDER THE WALKER'S FEET until the terrain extends south.

persons.name: Russel E. Heacock
persons.note: THE ONE VOTE AGAINST THE TOWN. He cast the single 'against incorporation' ballot on 5 August 1833 - Andreas prints the poll - 'he living at that time beyond the extreme southern border of the proposed town, although having his business and professional interests at the settlement. He moved into the town the following year.' Andreas calls it 'exceptional fidelity to conviction and independence of opinion'. He received one hundred dollars at the Indian treaty of 26 September 1833 and was among the original subscribers to the Chicago Democrat in November 1833. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 13 times, as “HEACOCK RUSSEL E”, “HEACOCK RUSSELL E”, 1833-10-22 to 1835-06-26: 3 federal land entries — E2NW sec 32 T39N R14E; E2SE sec 34 T39N R13E; W2NE sec 32 T39N R14E and 8 parcels of the school section — BL129 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read; BL20 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read; BL30 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read; BL61 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read; BL9 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read; lot 2 of block 23 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 7 of block 117 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 7 of block 25 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), 417.29 acres stated in all, for $1145.00 (ls0230, ls0231, ls0232, ls0233, ls0234, ls0235, ls0236, ls0237, ls0475, ls0476, ls0477, ls0478, ls0869). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS COOK, UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE SCHOOL-SECTION ROWS ARE GROUND INSIDE THE TOWN, NOT FARMLAND: section 16 of T39N R14E was platted and sold off by lot and by block at the sale of 1833, which is why the register states 0000.00 acres against most of them. Ground inside the town is nearer to this reconstruction than a quarter-section is, and it is still a purchase: the register names a purchaser and never an occupant, and nothing here puts this person on that ground. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. The register states this purchaser's residence as COOK, so the sale is contemporary evidence that a man of this name lived in Cook County on the date of sale. It is not evidence that he lived in the town. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: HEACOCK RUSSEL E matches Russel E. Heacock: the forename names Russel E. Heacock of the 1 person of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

persons.name: Heacock's wife and children, unnamed
persons.note: COUNTED INDIRECTLY AND NOT NAMED. Andreas: he removed in 1834 'that his children might be nearer school', into a house on the east bank of the South Branch a little south of Randolph Street; in the spring of 1835 he built a house on what he supposed was his lot and 'Here his fifth son and youngest child was born'; and in the cholera of 1849 'he fled with his family to a farm he owned at Summit, where he himself, his wife, and two sons were attacked, and died in quick succession'. So the household on 1 July 1835 contains a wife and at least five sons. THE SOURCE COUNTS THEM AND NAMES NONE, so they are one placeholder entry and not seven invented people. Do not count this entry as a person.

residents.research_note: THE OLDEST RESIDENCE, THE ONLY VOTE AGAINST THE TOWN, AND THE LARGEST DOCUMENTED HOUSEHOLD IN THE PARCEL - a wife and five sons, the youngest born in the spring of 1835. It is also the record that best shows why the population layer must precede the building layer: this household of seven had a house built in the season before the scene date, at a street address, which the model does not contain. THE PROJECT SHOULD NOT LOSE THE ROLLERS. A documented instance of a Chicago house being moved bodily one block in 1835 is evidence about construction, weight and the town's attitude to its own buildings, and it belongs in the K4 facades work as much as here.
